quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It is not necessary before every ride

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which type of sign is usually rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. They show traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: Which action will NOT prevent someone from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them
Keep them busy with activities while they sober up
Let them wait 15 minutes after their last drink, then drive
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them wait 15 minutes after their last drink, then drive
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, and get friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes does not make it safe to drive.

questions.question: Why should riders not rely only on their mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are too small to see much
Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles
Using mirrors takes your eyes off the road ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. Do not rely only on mirrors. Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder regularly.

questions.question: What should you do on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy
Ride more than 12 hours each day

questions.explanation: Wear warm clothes to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take rest breaks every 2 hours. Caffeine only causes worse tiredness later.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycle riders and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where riders and other drivers are most likely to conflict. Use extra caution when entering and crossing intersections.

questions.question: Why should cargo be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: High cargo raises the center of gravity
High cargo might block the turn signals
You cannot see over high cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: High cargo raises the center of gravity
questions.explanation: Placing cargo too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles at night. Use your high beam when you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to daytime?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night
Allow a shorter following distance at night
Keep the same following distance at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it hard to judge distance because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Stay farther behind other vehicles at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Help other riders see you better.
Do not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other riders see you better.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is a good choice. It protects you in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at the same time.

questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time on a two-lane road. Each rider must finish their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Drifting into another lane while turning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: Entering a turn at too high a speed can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not puff up when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not puff up when riding.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits made for motorcycles will not tear or puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: Slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel very smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire will make steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake hard, then slowly increase the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use the front and rear brakes together at the same time.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. If another hazard appears, you may have no way to escape. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT give the best protection if it:
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no defects. Cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps reduce protection.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay safe. Position yourself to avoid blind spots, see and be seen better, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and have an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide good wind protection.
